# Interoperability: federating without surrendering the canonical model

Quarto-Needs treats interchange and federation as projections and adapters around the canonical engineering graph. External standards may transport, describe, or discover requirements, but they do not become a second semantic authority.

## Driver and obligations

::: {.need #STK-006 type="stakeholder-need" status="approved" tags="interoperability;oslc;federation;standards"}
## Engineering teams need standards-based federation without semantic drift

Teams need to exchange and discover requirements through established standards while preserving canonical identity, provenance, trust, and explicit loss semantics.
:::

::: {.need #SYS-007 type="system-requirement" status="approved" priority="high" tags="interoperability;oslc;federation;provenance" derives-from="STK-006" implemented-by="COMP-OSLC" verified-by="TC-015;TC-016;TC-017;TC-018;TC-019"}
## Federate OSLC requirements through a bounded read-only adapter

Quarto-Needs shall discover OSLC Requirements Management services, execute explicitly selected read-only Query Capabilities, materialize selected query members as independently provenance-bearing observations, and reconcile observed external resources through a bounded federation layer that preserves external identity, cache provenance, and trust without importing remote semantics into the canonical graph automatically.

### Rationale

Federation is useful only if remote state remains distinguishable from authored project truth and failures remain explainable.
:::

::: {.need #FUN-010 type="functional-requirement" status="approved" priority="high" tags="oslc;http;cache;rdf;discovery" derives-from="SYS-007" implemented-by="COMP-OSLC;IF-005" verified-by="TC-015" mitigates="RISK-005"}
## Discover OSLC RM services and advertised Resource Shapes

The federation adapter shall fetch a configured Service Provider through bounded GET-only HTTP, normalize supported RDF representations without implicit network dereferencing, discover RM Query Capabilities, and fetch advertised Resource Shapes through the same cache and transport policy.

### Rationale

Discovery, RDF parsing, transport, and cache semantics must be explicit and independently testable before remote requirement import is considered.
:::

::: {.need #FUN-011 type="functional-requirement" status="approved" priority="high" tags="oslc;reconciliation;identity;conflict" derives-from="SYS-007" implemented-by="COMP-OSLC" verified-by="TC-016;TC-019" mitigates="RISK-005"}
## Reconcile external requirements only through explicit identity bindings

Quarto-Needs shall compare observed external requirements with canonical objects without mutating either side and shall treat an explicit external-resource-URI to canonical-ID binding as the only identity bridge. Matching titles or external identifiers shall never create an implicit merge.

### Rationale

Provider identifiers and display fields can be reused, mutable, or locally ambiguous. Reconciliation must surface unbound resources, stale or rejected observations, missing local targets, duplicate bindings, and field differences before any future import operation is allowed.
:::

::: {.need #FUN-012 type="functional-requirement" status="approved" priority="high" tags="oslc;query;query-capability;read-only;bounded" derives-from="SYS-007" implemented-by="COMP-OSLC;IF-005" verified-by="TC-017" mitigates="RISK-005"}
## Execute an explicitly selected OSLC Query Capability without crawling members

Quarto-Needs shall execute a bounded HTTP GET against an explicitly selected OSLC Query Capability, parse the query-result container deterministically, enforce a maximum member count, preserve query-response provenance, and report member URIs without recursively dereferencing them.

### Rationale

Discovery is not sufficient for practical federation, but query execution must not silently turn into unbounded Linked Data crawling. Query results therefore remain a resource-discovery projection; authoritative member observation is a separate bounded operation.
:::

::: {.need #FUN-013 type="functional-requirement" status="approved" priority="high" tags="oslc;observation;provenance;member-fetch;bounded" derives-from="SYS-007" implemented-by="COMP-OSLC;IF-005" verified-by="TC-018;TC-019" mitigates="RISK-005"}
## Materialize selected OSLC query members as independently provenance-bearing observations

Quarto-Needs shall fetch query-member URIs individually through the existing bounded transport/cache policy, normalize each fetched representation, enforce explicit fan-out and per-resource node limits, and create external requirement observations whose digest, retrieval time, trust state, validators, and resource identity derive from the bytes actually observed for that member.

### Rationale

A query container may include inline member data, but its response digest is not the digest of every member resource. Independent retrieval preserves the provenance boundary required for trustworthy reconciliation and any future reviewed import plan.
:::

::: {.need #NFR-006 type="non-functional-requirement" status="approved" priority="critical" tags="oslc;security;provenance;offline;determinism" derives-from="SYS-007" implemented-by="COMP-OSLC" verified-by="TC-015;TC-016;TC-017;TC-018;TC-019" mitigates="RISK-005"}
## Keep federation bounded, provenance-preserving, and fail-explicit

OSLC federation shall enforce byte/time/redirect/node/member budgets, reject cross-origin redirects, prevent implicit remote JSON-LD context loading and recursive member crawling, preserve content digests and historical observations, distinguish query-response provenance from member-resource provenance, and never hide authentication failures or identity conflicts behind stale cache fallback or heuristic matching.

### Rationale

External integration expands the trust boundary and therefore requires stronger failure, provenance, identity, and traversal contracts than local projection alone.
:::

::: {.need #STK-007 type="stakeholder-need" status="approved" tags="interoperability;github;issues;tracker"}
## Engineering teams need requirements linked to live issue-tracker state without importing the tracker

Teams need read-only visibility into GitHub issue state — discovery, bounded traversal, and normalized observations — while GitHub remains an external source whose identity, provenance, and trust boundaries stay outside the canonical graph.
:::

::: {.need #SYS-008 type="system-requirement" status="approved" priority="high" tags="interoperability;github;issues;provenance" derives-from="STK-007" implemented-by="COMP-GHISSUES" verified-by="TC-020;TC-021;TC-022;TC-023;TC-024"}
## Federate GitHub issues as read-only, provenance-bound observations

Quarto-Needs shall fetch GitHub issues through bounded GET-only HTTP, normalize them into the same external-observation shape OSLC federation uses, discover and traverse issue-list pages within explicit budgets, and reconcile observed issues through explicit API-URI-to-canonical-ID bindings — never promoting issue numbers, HTML URLs, or inline list data into canonical identity.

### Rationale

GitHub issues carry engineering-relevant state, but the tracker is mutable, paginated, rate-limited, and mixes pull requests into its issue listings — federation therefore needs bounded budgets, exact-byte provenance, and explicit separation between discovery and observation.
:::

::: {.need #FUN-014 type="functional-requirement" status="approved" priority="high" tags="github;issues;identity;projection;provenance" derives-from="SYS-008" implemented-by="COMP-GHISSUES" verified-by="TC-020" mitigates="RISK-005;RISK-012"}
## Normalize fetched GitHub issues without creating canonical identity

The GitHub adapter shall normalize a fetched issue payload into an external requirement observation whose digest, retrieval time, and validators derive from the bytes actually fetched, reject pull requests explicitly, keep the issue number as data-only external identity, and treat null or missing fields without guessing.
:::

::: {.need #FUN-015 type="functional-requirement" status="approved" priority="high" tags="github;http;cache;conditional-requests" derives-from="SYS-008" implemented-by="COMP-GHISSUES;IF-006" verified-by="TC-021" mitigates="RISK-005"}
## Fetch GitHub issues through a bounded, cached, conditional transport

The GitHub adapter shall compose the bounded GET-only transport with an opt-in content-addressed cache: a fresh cached representation shall skip the network entirely, a stale entry shall send conditional validators built from its own stored metadata, and a 304 response shall reuse the cached body under refreshed provenance instead of re-downloading it.
:::

::: {.need #FUN-016 type="functional-requirement" status="approved" priority="high" tags="github;discovery;pagination;bounded;read-only" derives-from="SYS-008" implemented-by="COMP-GHISSUES;IF-006" verified-by="TC-022" mitigates="RISK-012"}
## Discover and traverse issue-list pages within explicit budgets

The GitHub adapter shall report discovered issue and pull-request numbers separately for one bounded list page, follow the server-provided Link rel="next" target only within an explicit page budget and the request origin, report truncation honestly when the budget stops a traversal that could continue, fail loudly on malformed pagination headers, and never promote inline list data into provenance-bound observations.
:::

::: {.need #FUN-017 type="functional-requirement" status="approved" priority="high" tags="github;reconciliation;identity;import;review" derives-from="SYS-008" implemented-by="COMP-GHISSUES;COMP-OSLC" verified-by="TC-023" mitigates="RISK-005"}
## Reconcile GitHub observations through the shared explicit-binding contracts

Observed GitHub issues shall reconcile and import-plan through the same source-agnostic reconciliation and reviewed import-plan contracts OSLC uses: an explicit external-API-URI to canonical-ID binding is the only identity bridge; a matching issue number, title, or HTML URL shall never create an implicit merge; and every planned directive remains a non-mutating review artifact carrying the observation's own provenance.
:::

::: {.need #NFR-007 type="non-functional-requirement" status="approved" priority="critical" tags="github;security;provenance;rate-limit;bounded" derives-from="SYS-008" implemented-by="COMP-GHISSUES" verified-by="TC-020;TC-021;TC-022;TC-024" mitigates="RISK-012"}
## Keep GitHub federation bounded, provenance-preserving, and rate-limit-explicit

GitHub federation shall enforce byte/time/redirect/page budgets, reject cross-origin redirect and pagination targets, and distinguish rate-limit exhaustion (a 403 carrying X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, or any 429) from authentication failures — reporting the server's retry facts to the caller instead of sleeping implicitly or hiding exhaustion behind generic errors.
:::

## Architecture

::: {.need #COMP-OSLC type="component" status="implemented" tags="oslc;federation;interoperability;python"}
## OSLC federation subsystem

Coordinates OSLC projection, external identity, deterministic cache persistence, bounded HTTP transport, RDF normalization, RM discovery, Resource Shape parsing, explicit query execution, member observation materialization, and non-mutating reconciliation without surrendering the canonical engineering graph.
:::

::: {.need #IF-005 type="interface" status="implemented" tags="oslc;http;rdf;federation"}
## Read-only OSLC federation interface

The adapter boundary accepts configured HTTP(S) Service Provider identity, explicit cache/fetch/query/observation policies, optional request-only authentication headers, and returns discovered RM services, Resource Shapes, bounded query results, and independently provenance-bearing external observations.
:::

::: {.need #RISK-005 type="risk" status="approved" priority="critical" tags="oslc;security;federation;credentials;stale-cache"}
## External federation leaks credentials or silently trusts stale, changed, misidentified, or unbounded remote data

Redirects, remote contexts, mutable resources, stale cache, opaque network failure, heuristic identity matching, query-container/member provenance confusion, or recursive member traversal could leak authentication material or make unverified external state appear canonical.
:::

::: {.need #ADR-008 type="architecture-decision" status="accepted" date="2026-08-30" revisit-after="2027-08-30" decision-makers="Quarto-Needs maintainers" tags="oslc;federation;read-only;security" addresses="SYS-007;FUN-010;FUN-012;FUN-013;NFR-006;RISK-005" applies-to="COMP-OSLC;IF-005" confirmed-by="TC-015;TC-017;TC-018;TC-019"}
## Keep the first OSLC federation path read-only, bounded, and cache-provenanced

### Context and Problem Statement

OSLC introduces external identity, authentication, mutable remote representations, linked-data serialization, caching, query capabilities, and provider-specific failure modes. Treating those concerns as ordinary local objects or automatically traversing every discovered link would blur the trust boundary.

### Decision Drivers

- preserve the canonical Quarto-Needs graph as semantic authority;
- make external identity and observed bytes independently auditable;
- prevent hidden network activity during RDF normalization;
- prevent credentials from crossing redirect origins or entering persistent artifacts;
- support deterministic offline behavior without silently accepting stale state;
- prevent discovery/query execution from becoming recursive Linked Data crawling;
- distinguish query-container evidence from independently fetched member-resource evidence.

### Decision Outcome

Implement OSLC as a read-only adapter. HTTP uses GET only with explicit budgets and same-origin redirects. Cached bytes are content-addressed by SHA-256 and historical observations are retained. RDF normalization performs no implicit remote context fetches. Query execution requires an explicitly selected query base, limits member count, and reports member URIs without recursively fetching them. A separate bounded observation step may fetch selected members individually and records provenance from each member's actual representation bytes. Discovery, query results, member observations, Resource Shapes, and reconciliation inputs remain external projections and are not merged into the canonical graph.

### Consequences

The adapter can discover, query, observe, and analyze reconciliation safely before synchronization exists. Canonical import and all remote writes remain deliberately deferred.

### Confirmation

`TC-015` exercises the complete network-free discovery orchestration path; `TC-017` exercises bounded query execution and response provenance; `TC-018` exercises independent member observation and per-resource provenance; `TC-019` exercises the reviewed, non-mutating import-plan directives derived from that observation and reconciliation.
:::

::: {.need #ADR-009 type="architecture-decision" status="accepted" date="2026-08-30" revisit-after="2027-08-30" decision-makers="Quarto-Needs maintainers" tags="oslc;reconciliation;identity;conflict" addresses="FUN-011;NFR-006;RISK-005" applies-to="COMP-OSLC" confirmed-by="TC-016"}
## Require explicit URI-to-canonical-ID bindings for OSLC reconciliation

### Context and Problem Statement

A remote OSLC requirement can expose an identifier or title that happens to match a local object even when the two resources are unrelated. Automatically treating such similarity as identity would permit silent aliasing across independent authorities.

### Decision Drivers

- preserve external resource URI as the primary remote identity;
- make every bridge into canonical identity explicit and reviewable;
- reject stale or rejected observations before reconciliation;
- expose duplicate bindings and missing local targets as conflicts;
- keep comparison separate from mutation.

### Decision Outcome

Reconciliation is a pure analysis step. Only an explicit mapping from external resource URI to canonical Quarto-Needs ID can yield a matched item. External identifiers and titles are comparison data only. Unbound resources remain unbound, and field differences are reported without changing the snapshot.

### Consequences

This is intentionally more conservative than heuristic import. A future import command may consume an accepted reconciliation plan, but it cannot infer identity by itself and it cannot bypass provenance/trust checks.

### Confirmation

`TC-016` proves that a matching external identifier alone remains unbound and therefore cannot create an implicit canonical identity.
:::

::: {.need #COMP-GHISSUES type="component" status="implemented" tags="github;federation;interoperability;python"}
## GitHub issues federation subsystem

Coordinates GitHub issue identity, bounded HTTP transport with rate-limit classification, content-addressed caching, conditional requests, issue-list discovery, bounded multi-page traversal, and normalization into OSLC's shared external-observation shape without surrendering the canonical engineering graph.
:::

::: {.need #IF-006 type="interface" status="implemented" tags="github;http;issues;federation"}
## Read-only GitHub issues adapter interface

The adapter boundary accepts configured owner/repository identity, explicit fetch/cache/page budgets, the list endpoint's own filter parameters, optional request-only authentication headers, and an injectable transport; it returns discovered issue and pull-request numbers per page, honest truncation reports, and independently provenance-bearing external observations, and raises distinguished errors for authentication, availability, and rate-limit exhaustion.
:::

::: {.need #RISK-012 type="risk" status="approved" priority="high" tags="github;security;pagination;rate-limit;traversal"}
## Unbounded pagination, silent truncation, or rate-limit blindness makes external state look canonical

Following server-provided pagination URLs without budgets or origin checks, reading a malformed pagination header as the end of the list, conflating pull requests with issues, promoting inline list data into observations, or misclassifying rate-limit exhaustion as an authentication failure could silently misrepresent external state or hide exhaustion behind the wrong error.
:::

::: {.need #ADR-010 type="architecture-decision" status="accepted" date="2026-08-31" revisit-after="2027-08-31" decision-makers="Quarto-Needs maintainers" tags="github;federation;read-only;security" addresses="SYS-008;FUN-014;FUN-015;FUN-016;NFR-007;RISK-012" applies-to="COMP-GHISSUES;IF-006" confirmed-by="TC-020;TC-021;TC-022;TC-024"}
## Keep the GitHub issues path read-only, bounded, and discovery-separated

### Context and Problem Statement

GitHub's issues API returns pull requests alongside issues, rewrites pagination URLs from `/repos/{owner}/{repo}` to `/repositories/{id}` with cursor parameters, includes full inline issue data in list responses, and rate-limits clients with 403/429 responses. Treating any of those as canonical requirements data, following pagination without budgets, or flattening rate limits into generic errors would blur the trust boundary.

### Decision Drivers

- reuse OSLC's source-agnostic identity, observation, reconciliation, and import-plan contracts instead of forking them;
- keep discovered numbers separate from independently fetched, provenance-bound observations;
- validate server-provided pagination targets by origin, never by path, because GitHub legitimately rewrites its own Link targets;
- make truncation, malformed pagination, pull-request conflation, and rate-limit exhaustion explicit rather than guessed;
- keep the transport free of retry policy: report the server's retry facts and let the caller decide.

### Decision Outcome

GitHub federation is a read-only adapter composed of a bounded JSON transport with rate-limit classification, an opt-in content-addressed cache with conditional requests, issue/projection normalization that rejects pull requests, discovery and bounded multi-page traversal that stay numbers-only, and reconciliation/import planning through the unchanged OSLC contracts. List data is never promoted into observations; pagination targets are origin-checked; rate limits raise a distinguished, retry-informing error.

### Consequences

The adapter can discover, traverse, observe, reconcile, and plan imports safely before any synchronization exists. Canonical import and all remote writes remain deliberately deferred, and a rate-limit retry policy is caller-owned until a command needs one.

### Confirmation

`TC-020` exercises fetch-compose-normalize with exact-byte provenance; `TC-021` exercises the conditional-request 304 reuse path; `TC-022` exercises bounded traversal across GitHub's rewritten pagination targets with honest truncation; `TC-024` exercises rate-limit exhaustion classification against real header shapes.
:::

## GitHub issues adapter slice

```text
STK-007
   ↓
SYS-008
   ├── FUN-014 / NFR-007 → ADR-010 → SRC-GITHUB-ISSUES            → TC-020 → EVD-020
   ├── FUN-015 / NFR-007 → ADR-010 → SRC-GITHUB-HTTP / -ISSUES    → TC-021 → EVD-021
   ├── FUN-016 / NFR-007 → ADR-010 → SRC-GITHUB-ISSUES / -HTTP    → TC-022 → EVD-022
   └── FUN-017           → ADR-010 → shared OSLC reconcile/import → TC-023 → EVD-023
                                                    SRC-GITHUB-HTTP → TC-024 → EVD-024
```

`FUN-017` deliberately implements against `SRC-OSLC-RECONCILE`/`SRC-OSLC-IMPORT`: the reconciliation and import-plan modules are source-agnostic, so GitHub observations flow through the unchanged OSLC contracts, and the slice's proof is tests pinning that reuse rather than a fork.
